faq.a: Abdulhalim is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم, whose core sense is abdulhalim; servant of the forbearing.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulhalim?
faq.a: Abdulhalim is associated with Arabic. Abdulhalim is Arabic عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم (ʿAbd al-Ḥalīm), meaning 'servant of the Forbearing'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم is Arabic.
Abdulhalim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulhalim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Ḥalīm is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdulhalim mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Abdulhalim mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdulhalim is rendered عبدالحلیم and carries the sense عبدالحلیم، بنده حلیم.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-dul-ha-lim. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdulhalim, abdulhalim. Script forms are عبدالحليم, عبدالحلیم, عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم, अब्दुलहलीम.
